body_markdown:
Vibely is an AI-powered app builder that lets users create web and mobile applications through natural language prompts. According to the 2026 Developer Survey,[65.9% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) reported using AI coding assistants or coding agents at work. For founders and creators exploring AI app builders, understanding the available options helps identify which platform fits their project, budget, and technical preferences.[Floot](https://floot.com/en) offers a different approach: a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector for building through supported AI assistants while Floot manages the app infrastructure.


This guide examines six Vibely alternatives through the lens of non-technical founders, solo creators, and small teams who want to ship working applications without traditional development overhead.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build through existing AI assistants** : Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) works with Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Available tools depend on the client's connector permissions, and connector-based code generation does not consume Floot AI build credits.
- **Daily action limits reset** : Floot's[building action limits](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-actions) provide 1,000 actions per day on Pro, with a reset every 24 hours. Hosting is metered separately after included allowances.
- **Full-stack infrastructure is managed** : Floot provides a[PostgreSQL database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , authentication, storage, hosting, email, and payment integration options, reducing the need to assemble those services independently.
- **Mobile publishing requires developer accounts** : Floot's[mobile app workflow](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) creates installable iOS and Android builds without local Xcode or Android Studio, but app-store accounts and approval remain necessary.
- **You retain ownership** : Floot's[code export options](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) distinguish code and data ownership on every plan from full project ZIP downloads, which require a paid plan.


## **Understanding AI App Builders and Your Needs**


AI app builders turn natural language descriptions into web or mobile applications. Rather than writing code line by line, users describe what they want to build, and AI tools generate interfaces, data models, and backend logic according to each platform's capabilities.


The core evaluation criteria for AI app builders include:


- **AI billing model** : Whether the platform uses its own AI credits or connects to assistants you already pay for
- **Infrastructure completeness** : Built-in databases, authentication, hosting, and email versus requiring external services
- **Code ownership** : Ability to export and self-host your application elsewhere
- **Mobile app support** : Web-only output versus native mobile generation or installable app packaging
- **Pricing structure** : Credit-based consumption versus subscription plans with separate action or usage limits


Vibely supports React Native mobile development and offers Supabase database integration on paid plans. The alternatives below take different approaches to conversational app development. Prices are in USD for monthly billing where specified, checked November 23, 2026, and may change.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/blog/vibecode-with-floot-bolt-replit-lovable-alternative) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected assistant handles development through the tools its client permits, while Floot manages hosting, databases, authentication, storage, and deployment. Floot complements these assistants and coding tools rather than replacing them.


### **Key Capabilities**


Floot combines a conversational development workflow with managed infrastructure for apps that need user accounts, saved data, and a live URL. Builders can use an existing AI assistant or Floot's own editor, while the[connector documentation](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) explains which actions remain in the browser.


- **MCP connector architecture** : Supported assistants can create and edit project files, run database operations, test, and publish when their connector permissions allow it.
- **Three build paths** : Connect an existing AI assistant, use the in-app editor with Floot's optional AI agent, or work through compatible coding clients such as Cursor and Codex.
- **Managed PostgreSQL** : A[built-in database](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) supports SQL, a browser-based table view, and database export on every plan.
- **Authentication brokering** :[App sign-in](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/app-sign-in) supports email/password and Google or Microsoft sign-in without separate OAuth app registration for those two providers.
- **Mobile app packaging** :[Mobile builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) produce installable iOS and Android apps and support submission to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks.


### **Pricing Structure**


Floot is free to start. The following monthly plan amounts and action limits match[Floot's pricing](https://floot.com/en/pricing) ; mobile-build quantities follow the current mobile documentation.


- **Free** : $0/month, 100 build actions/day, 2 mobile builds/month, and a one-time $3 hosting credit
- **Pro** : $25/month, 1,000 daily actions, 5,000 monthly AI credits, $10 monthly hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds/month, and custom domains
- **Power** : $100/month, 5,000 daily actions, 15,000 monthly AI credits, $25 monthly hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds


Annual billing offers two months free. AI credits can be used for Floot's optional agent, image generation, or in-app AI features. Connector-based code generation uses the connected assistant's own model allowance, but image generation may still consume Floot credits. Hosting beyond included allowances draws from prepaid credit, and auto-reload is optional.


### **Why Floot Stands Out as the Best Vibely Alternative**


For users who already subscribe to a supported AI assistant, Floot avoids a separate Floot AI build-credit charge for connector-based code generation. Assistant subscription limits and Floot's daily build-action limits still apply. This setup is relevant to founders who need a working app without configuring database servers, authentication, and hosting individually.


Floot has a[4.8/5 G2 rating](https://www.g2.com/sellers/floot) , based on eight reviews as of November 2026. Its managed services also include email sending, SEO controls, and visitor analytics. Sending email to customers requires a verified sending domain on a paid plan, as explained in the[email guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/email) .


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is an AI app builder that generates web applications from natural language descriptions. The platform supports rapid prototyping and full-stack web applications.


### **Primary Focus**


- **UI generation** : Produces web interfaces and supports iterative visual changes
- **Full-stack web development** : Supports web applications with backend functionality
- **GitHub integration** : Offers two-way code synchronization and version control
- **Collaboration features** : Unlimited collaborators across plans, with additional workspace controls on Business
- **Credit-based AI usage** : Combines monthly plan credits with daily grants


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free** : $0/month, 5 daily credits with a cap of 30 monthly credits
- **Pro** : $25/month, 100 monthly credits plus daily grants
- **Business** : $50/month, 100 monthly credits plus team workspace controls


### **Platform Overview**


Lovable has more than 400 G2 reviews and a 4.6/5 rating as of November 2026. It supports interface iteration, GitHub synchronization, and on-demand credit top-ups on paid plans. For another perspective on infrastructure and connector-based billing, see the[Floot vs Lovable](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-lovable-compare-ai-no-code-platforms-2025) comparison.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based AI app builder focused on moving from prompts to working applications. It supports prototyping and iterative web development without local environment setup.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Fast prototyping** : Prompt-to-running-app workflows in the browser
- **Browser-based development** : No local installation required to begin
- **Expo mobile support** : Mobile development workflows based on Expo
- **Token-based pricing** : Usage measured in tokens consumed
- **Built-in database** : Bolt Database supports persistent application data


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free** : $0/month, up to 1 million tokens/month with a 300,000-token daily limit
- **Pro** : $25/month, starting at 10 million tokens/month with no daily token limit


### **Platform Overview**


Bolt.new suits users who prefer building directly in the browser and refining an application through prompts. Token consumption varies with project size and the scope of each requested change. The[Floot vs Bolt](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) guide discusses differences in building workflows and managed infrastructure.


## **4. Replit Agent**


Replit Agent combines AI-assisted development with a cloud development environment. It serves users who want a prompt-driven workflow alongside code editing, debugging, and collaboration tools.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Complete cloud IDE** : Code editing, terminal access, and debugging tools
- **AI Agent integration** : Natural-language development within the cloud environment
- **Expo mobile support** : Mobile previews and guided iOS App Store submission
- **Git integration** : Version control for application development
- **Usage-based pricing** : AI Agent tasks use effort-based pricing, with separate deployment and infrastructure usage costs


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free tier** : Basic development resources and limited AI usage
- **Core** : $20/month with included AI usage allowance and potential additional usage charges
- **Pro** : $100/month with higher AI allowances and collaboration features


### **Platform Overview**


Replit Agent supports builders who want both AI assistance and direct access to development tools. Its cloud environment and collaboration features are useful when projects require hands-on code changes. See the[Floot vs Replit](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) comparison for a closer look at different infrastructure approaches.


## **5. Base44**


Base44 is an AI app builder that became part of Wix following an acquisition in June 2025. It continues to offer AI-led app creation workflows.


### **Primary Focus**


- **AI-driven development** : Natural-language app generation
- **Wix ownership** : Acquired by Wix in June 2025 while continuing as a distinct AI app-building product
- **Full-stack capabilities** : Frontend and backend generation
- **Code export** : Access to generated application code


### **Pricing Structure**


- **Free** : $0/month, 25 message credits and 100 integration credits per month
- **Starter** : $20/month, 100 message credits and 2,000 integration credits per month
- **Builder** : $50/month, 250 message credits and 10,000 integration credits per month
- **Pro** : $100/month, 500 message credits and 20,000 integration credits per month
- **Elite** : $200/month, 1,200 message credits and 50,000 integration credits per month


### **Platform Overview**


Base44 offers natural-language application generation and integrated backend functionality. Its Wix acquisition does not, by itself, establish integration with every Wix service. For a Floot-focused comparison of app-building approaches, see[Floot vs Base44](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


## **6. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets eligible ChatGPT users create, preview, and publish interactive websites and lightweight web applications within ChatGPT. It provides a hosted workflow for turning natural-language prompts into shareable experiences.


### **Primary Focus**


- **ChatGPT-native building** : Create and refine hosted websites and lightweight apps through ChatGPT
- **Persistent data** : Supports relational databases, file storage, and access-controlled applications
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish without configuring a separate web hosting provider
- **Web application focus** : Intended for hosted web experiences rather than native app-store submission
- **Usage-based limits** : Building and editing count toward Codex allowances, while hosting and storage have separate limits


### **Pricing Structure**


ChatGPT Sites is available through eligible ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise plans rather than a separate Sites subscription. Building and editing count toward Codex usage. Hosting is currently included with Plus and Pro, while Enterprise hosting charges are currently waived; usage limits and workspace terms still apply.


### **Platform Overview**


ChatGPT Sites suits users who want to build and publish web experiences inside ChatGPT. It uses its own hosting and storage environment rather than Floot's managed PostgreSQL stack and mobile app-building workflow. Sites permits e-commerce through third-party payment processors, but cannot directly handle payment-card data. Site owners are responsible for configuring and maintaining those integrations.


## **Key Features to Evaluate in a Vibely Alternative**


When comparing AI app builders, several factors affect project requirements and long-term maintenance:


### **AI Billing Model**


Different platforms approach AI usage pricing in distinct ways:


- **Connector-based** : Uses an existing AI assistant's allowance for code generation, while Floot separately meters[build actions](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-actions) and hosting; image generation and optional AI features can consume Floot credits
- **Credit-based** : Monthly credit allocations that may require top-ups
- **Token-based** : Consumption tied to generation volume
- **Usage-based** : AI activity and infrastructure charges alongside subscriptions


### **Infrastructure Completeness**


Platforms vary in which services are managed and which require configuration:


- **Database** : Managed PostgreSQL, Supabase integration, or platform-specific solutions
- **Authentication** : Built-in OAuth brokering versus provider setup
- **Hosting** : Included allowances versus metered usage and separate hosting costs
- **Email** : Built-in sending capabilities versus third-party integration


### **Code and Data Ownership**


Code and data export options vary across platforms, and exporting application code does not necessarily include the underlying database or uploaded files. Floot provides[code and data ownership](https://floot.com/blog/do-you-own-your-code-on-floot) on every plan, with database export on all tiers and full project ZIP downloads on paid plans. Review the export options before deciding how you would move an app to another host.


## **Why Floot Delivers the Best Alternative to Vibely**


Floot is a fit for founders who already use an AI assistant and want to build a working application without setting up the infrastructure themselves. Through its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) , supported clients can create, edit, and publish projects, subject to their connector permissions. Floot manages what the application runs on, while the connected assistant handles development.


- **Existing AI access** : Connector-based code generation uses the assistant's model allowance rather than a separate Floot AI build-credit bill.
- **Managed backend** : PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, email, payments integration, and hosting are available within Floot.
- **Mobile delivery** :[iOS and Android builds](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) can reach testing tracks without a local Mac, although developer accounts and app-store approval are still required.
- **Daily build capacity** : Actions reset daily, with plan-dependent caps and separate usage-based hosting costs.
- **Ownership** : App code and data belong to the builder, while full ZIP downloads require a paid plan.


For[non-technical founders](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) building client portals, internal tools, or apps with saved data, this combination offers a practical path from a conversation to a published product.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What makes Floot different from other AI app builders?**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) that lets supported assistants handle development while Floot provides managed infrastructure. Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations can work with Floot, but available building actions depend on connector permissions. Connector-based code generation uses the connected assistant's allowance rather than Floot AI build credits, while daily action limits and hosting usage still apply.


### **Can I build mobile apps with these Vibely alternatives?**


Yes, although the methods differ. Floot[packages web apps](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) into installable iOS and Android builds and can send them to TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks. Replit and Bolt.new support Expo-based workflows, while Vibely builds with React Native and Expo. App-store publication is subject to developer-account requirements and store review; on Floot, connecting Google Play requires a paid plan.


### **How do credit-based and action-based pricing models compare?**


Credit-based services allocate credits or tokens to AI work, while Floot's[daily action model](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-actions) counts completed connector tool calls such as edits, reads, and tests. Pro provides 1,000 actions per day, with a reset every 24 hours. Floot AI credits apply separately to optional AI features and image generation. Hosting beyond included allowances draws from prepaid credit.


### **Do I own the code generated by AI app builders?**


Ownership and export rights differ by provider. With Floot, users retain code, data, and IP ownership on every plan, and the database can be exported on Free. Full project ZIP downloads require a paid plan. The[export guide](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) explains how to retrieve code and data and what to consider before self-hosting.


### **Which Vibely alternative is best for non-technical founders?**


For non-technical founders who already use a supported assistant, Floot's managed infrastructure and[connector workflow](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) can reduce separate setup work. Lovable emphasizes a conversational web-app workflow, while Replit also offers a cloud IDE. The best choice depends on whether the project needs a persistent database, authentication, mobile delivery, code export, and a billing model that matches expected usage.
